topics.title: 42.1 Parsing commands
topics.summary: Parsing begins with lexical rules for words, quoting, escapes, and operators. A space inside quotes is data, while an unquoted pipe character may be syntax. A quoted "|" must not become a pipeline operator merely because its final text is a vertical bar. Represent token kind separately from token text. Then build an abstract command structure containing argument vectors, ordered redirections, pipeline stages, and background status. Reject incomplete constructs before launch, including unterminated quotes and a redirection without a destination.

topics.title: 42.2 Creating processes
topics.summary: The executor creates the required children and tracks each successful creation. Failure halfway through a pipeline requires cleanup of descriptors and already-created children. The plan must define what happens to partially started work. Built-in commands complicate the model. A command such as changing the shell’s current directory must affect the shell process itself in the appropriate context; executing it only in a child would leave the parent unchanged. Decide which operations are built-ins before applying a blanket fork-everything rule.

topics.title: 42.3 Executing programs
topics.summary: Each child prepares descriptors, signal state, process-group membership, and other required context before exec. The argument vector should preserve parsed word boundaries. Exec failure must end the child branch with an appropriate status rather than return to the interactive shell loop. A secure launcher also defines executable lookup and environment handling. A general shell intentionally supports broad user-controlled behavior; an application that merely needs to run one helper should prefer direct argument-vector execution instead of implementing or invoking unnecessary shell syntax.

topics.title: 42.4 Redirection
topics.summary: Redirection modifies a command’s descriptor relationships in the order specified by the language. Input files, output truncation, append mode, and descriptor duplication require distinct operations. Do not postpone error checking until after exec. If opening a required input fails, the command cannot run as requested. The shell should report the setup error and avoid silently falling back to its own input stream.

topics.title: 42.5 Pipelines
topics.summary: A pipeline is a group of connected stages, not a sequence of complete programs run one after another. Its data flow requires overlap when bounded pipes connect producers and consumers. Track pipe-end ownership explicitly. For an N-stage pipeline, there are N−1 connecting pipes, but each child needs only its relevant input and output roles. Extra inherited ends must be closed so that EOF and broken-pipe behavior reflect the intended graph.

topics.title: 42.6 Foreground jobs
topics.summary: A foreground job receives the terminal relationship intended for interactive input and terminal-generated signals. The shell normally waits for the job’s completion or stop state before resuming its prompt. Waiting for one PID is insufficient for a pipeline treated as one job. The shell must track all member processes and determine when the job as a whole is complete or stopped. Status reporting is therefore a job-level state machine.

topics.summary: This lexer supports spaces, single and double quotes, simple backslash escaping, and the operators | , < , > , and & . Its double-quote escape rules are deliberately simpler than a full POSIX shell. It performs no expansion, substitution, execution, or redirection. Companion listing: ch42/lexer.py The explicit active flag preserves an empty quoted argument. Without it, echo "" could be reduced incorrectly to a one-word command. Typed tokens likewise preserve the difference between a quoted vertical bar and an actual pipeline operator. The next stage would validate token sequences and produce a command tree. Only after that validation should an executor allocate pipes or create children. This is an example of a broader systems principle: make invalid plans fail before acquiring external resources whenever practical.

A pipeline can place all of its child processes into one process group and make that group the terminal’s foreground group. Terminal-generated signals such as an interactive interrupt can then target the whole job. The shell waits for or monitors the group rather than treating each pipeline process as an unrelated command.
